sentences: A simple polygonalization orders a given planar point set around a polygon without crossing its edges.
The source asks whether the total number of such polygons can be computed in polynomial time.
Finding one polygon is much easier than accounting for every valid cyclic ordering.
The counting question is also related to generating a uniformly random polygon on the same vertices.
A sharp algorithmic classification would clarify whether geometric noncrossing structure can overcome the large combinatorial space of candidate tours.
